author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
Plato complained writing is bad for thinking

No too long ago, people complained typing is bad for thinking, you can think when you write with a pen

Now, people complains chatting with AI is bad for thinking, you can only think if you type the essay by hand.

Do you see a pattern?

author.name: Fred Thomas
author.headline: Senior Research Scientist at VIAVI Solutions

comments.text:
I'm a firm believer that writing by hand improves retention of information. In my college classes, I learned the material more effectively when I wrote it down from the chalkboard rather than when the professor used slides and gave us printouts. I still write my notes by hand. It's zero marginal cost because I foolishly bought a 2500-sheet box of dot matrix printer paper 30 years ago and I still have 25% of it left.

A.I. essays are inferior to anything that I would write, so only a loser would try that. Or are you talking about a guy named Al(bert)? With sans serif fonts that don't differentiate between AI and Al, you should use periods like I do.

author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Using AI building the chips that power the AI.

replies.text:
Fred Thomas If retention of details is what you are looking for, I complete agree with you. Writing with a pen is better.

But do we need to memorize those details with Google (never mind AI) You still need to remember how to recall those info when needed, but you don't need to remember the info itself.

author.name: Fred Thomas
author.headline: Senior Research Scientist at VIAVI Solutions

replies.text: Horace Chan Learning and using your brain prevents dementia. I've read articles and anecdotes saying that "use it or lose it" is a real consequence of relying on A.I..

author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Using AI building the chips that power the AI.

replies.text:
Fred Thomas using AI is actually more taxing to my brain than writing essay.

You have to think at one level above what the AI is thinking.

talk to all the AI-native engineers, they are all super busy and everyone's brain is fryed after using AI all day long.

author.name: Ann Thomas
author.headline: Billing and Collections Specialist at Cogent Communications

author.name: Douglas Rudder
author.headline: Developmental Editor at Manning Publications Co.

comments.text:
Nope; AI is not a true parallel with pen and keyboard. When writing by hand or with a keyboard, you are still thinking through every piece of content, using your own critical thinking and creative skills. Every word, every thought is yours.

That is part of how we learn. It goes beyond "retaining knowledge" to developing a deeper understanding.

You lose a big part of that when you outsource the heavy lifting to AI.
